text:
alex: I'm assembling a short migration guide that shows how teams move from ad-hoc autoscale YAMLs into the new dedicated provisioning flow. Will include small TF -> SDK mappings, a canary rollout checklist, and a tiny troubleshooting FAQ. Pushing a draft PR this afternoon. @riley @mira any red flags?

riley: Love it. Can we surface an explicit table for eviction scoring and label precedence? Ops still asks which label wins when tenant + isolation both present.

mira: Yes please. Example rule: tenant label > isolation label when tenant has reserved pool assignment; otherwise isolation drives eviction_score. Also show numeric eviction_score examples (0 = lowest eviction priority, 100 = highest).

alex: Good call. I'll include an explicit mapping snippet: isolation:dedicated -> eviction_score: 0; isolation:shared -> eviction_score: 80; tenant:analytics -> eviction_score: 10 (if assigned to reserved-pool).

sam: Add a blurb about how prefix/KV caching reduces CPU for repeated prefixes and can affect when reactive policies trigger; tiny note in troubleshooting is fine.

mira: For the SDK snippet, prefer Python + Go this time (Node already well-covered). I'll paste small Go example for createScalePolicy in a bit.

docs-bot: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4509 - dedicated-migration-guide. CI: docs-lint OK, linkcheck: 1 broken anchor.

alex: Which anchor? I want to avoid adding redirects if possible.

docs-bot: Broken anchor: /docs/dedicated/provisioning#canary-rollout-checklist -> anchor missing. Page updated recently.

riley: I'll add the anchor to the provisioning page and push a tiny follow-up, call it "canary-rollout-checklist".

alex: Great. I'll wait for that before merging. Also planning a short changelog section listing what examples were removed and where they went, so readers can find the old snippets.

mira: Go snippet here for inclusion:

```go
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("RW_KEY"))
_, err := client.Dedicated.CreateScalePolicy(context.Background(), redwood.CreateScalePolicyParams{
  PoolID: "pool-777", Name: "steady-75", Policy: redwood.Policy{Type: "steady", Targets: map[string]float64{"cpu":0.75}}
})
```

alex: Perfect. Tagging reviewers: @riley @mira @sam. Will merge once anchor fix lands and CI is green. ETA EOD. :rocket:
